title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1970-02-04
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway

ai_review.summary: Soundboard source with noticeable hiss and distortion, but the set shines thanks to a smoking Hard To Handle, exploratory China Rider and a solid Midnight Hour.
ai_review.review: The Kaplan SBD capture is marred by garbled, hissy sections and occasional drop‑outs that are typical of early‑70 recordings, yet it remains listenable for fans who appreciate analog warmth. Musically the show delivers strong moments – a fiery Hard To Handle, an adventurous China Rider and a respectable Midnight Hour – with Phil Lesh’s bass groove and Jerry Garcia’s soaring solos getting particular praise.

ai_rating.rationale: Average user rating (≈3.4) reflects a show that is musically decent but hampered by consistent recording flaws; enough detailed reviews allow a confident assessment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers repeatedly note distortion, hiss, garbled audio and occasional cuts, though some consider it acceptable for a 1970 SBD capture.

poor_songs: Midnight Hour (bogs down in later comments)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is described as short, tight and restrained with a notable jam after Midnight; overall solid but not spectacular compared to other Feb ’70 shows.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s solos are highlighted as “gliding over tribal funk” and his vocal on Black Peter is called one of his top deliveries.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh is praised for laying down a strong bass line with Santana‑style percussion during the post‑Midnight jam.
